1. Confirm the sizes on the dimension sheet (80 mm across, 100 mm tall, with guessed wall, floor and cell sizes).
2. Plan the cup's features (hexagon body, hollow with floor, honeycomb cutouts) and build them in steps.
3. Check the built part against the plan.
4. Slice the plate on the P1S (needs your OK to slice).
5. Send to the printer (needs your OK to queue, then start).

steps.text:
The pen cup is built and passes all four plan checks. It's an 80 mm across-corners hexagon, 100 mm tall, with a 2 mm side wall and a 3 mm floor. Six rows of 8 mm honeycomb cells, 2 mm ribs, are cut through each flat wall. The walls are watertight and the thinnest wall is 1.98 mm.

The guessed values are the 2 mm wall, 3 mm floor, 8 mm cells and 2 mm ribs. I also took 80 mm as across corners, so across flats is 69.3 mm. If you meant across flats, tell me and I'll rebuild it. I have not sliced or sent it to the P1S. Say the word when you want that.
